requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The specification occupies one page and explicitly records the burgundy colour code and audience introduction. It specifies the intact emblem and lettering, unchanged arrangement and proportions, uniform scaling, a light solid background and unobstructed visible bounds. It records the pattern's source colours, upright orientation and internal geometry, permitted cropping, repetition and uniform scaling, and the minimum complete dotted hollow diamond plus recognisable pale wave-band portion. Missing or contradictory specifications fail.

Treat the identity specification as the upstream authority for the rules board and applications. Exported files alone do not establish creation chronology; record this process requirement without inferring a chronological failure from filenames or presentation order.

The board demonstrates the supplied company assets in relation to production-title treatments and usable practical-information examples. Doors and performance are visibly distinct information categories. Layout and typography may vary, but an asset-only display or an example that confuses the two time categories fails.

Compare the company mark with 03-riverthread-wordmark.png and the motif with 04-costume-pattern.png. Each image must contain the complete burgundy emblem and lettering, with unchanged arrangement and proportions, on a light solid field and clear of overlap or clipping. The pattern must retain its gold, pale and deep-blue source colours, upright orientation and internal geometry. Cropping, repetition, fragment placement and uniform scaling are allowed, but each image must retain at least one whole hollow diamond with its central dot and a recognisable pale wave-band portion. Relettering, distortion, rotation, recolouring or missing minimum motif content fails.

Read the specification and confirm that all four images apply its complete-mark and minimum pattern treatments and print its audience introduction. Composition and scale may change to suit each application. A missing introduction or an application that contradicts the recorded asset rules fails; public applications need not print technical rule prose.

Read each material's venue, date and two separately labelled times. Alder materials must associate Alder Town Hall with 27 February 2027, doors 18:30 and performance 19:00; Bracken materials must associate Bracken Arts House with 6 March 2027, doors 14:30 and performance 15:00. Unambiguous equivalent English date and time formats are acceptable. Both tickets must visibly carry the sample-invalidity label, and both signs must use the entrance heading. Missing fields, swapped stop records or ambiguous time labels fail.

Both programme images identify the Alder opening on 27 February 2027. The spread preserves the full synopsis meaning: a young boat repairer borrows the town's only ceremonial lantern for a night repair, it disappears, a neighbour assumes it was sold, three encounters across the river reveal practical kindness, and returning it becomes a shared journey rather than a private apology. Paraphrasing is allowed without losing or reversing these events. Three distinguishable notes explain this production's voice, percussion and repeated-costume functions. Every text block stays entirely within one page; omitted story events, generic substitute notes or text crossing the centre divide fail.

The spread visibly comprises two landscape pages separated by a recognisable centre divide. It reads as a paired programme spread with the required production information, synopsis and notes, rather than a single undivided page. No exact pixel dimensions are required.

The guide uses Your first visit as its heading and visibly includes all three supplied guidance sentences: Check the venue and performance time on your ticket.; Doors open 30 minutes before the performance.; The performance includes a 10-minute interval. Preserve the original words and punctuation, allowing changes to capitalisation and line wrapping. Missing, paraphrased or contradictory guidance fails.

Each poster and the programme spread must identify English as the performance language and communicate a total duration of 90 minutes that includes one 10-minute interval. Each poster and ticket must state both general admission and unreserved seating. Capitalisation and layout may vary. An omitted required field, reserved-seat implication or interval presented as additional to the 90 minutes fails.

Review the complete video and its runtime. It must last 10 seconds, visibly use the delivered key visual, complete company mark and costume pattern, and include The Borrowed Lantern and Story, song and percussion. Each stop must have a separately readable information sequence: Alder Town Hall, 27 February 2027, doors 18:30, performance 19:00; Bracken Arts House, 6 March 2027, doors 14:30, performance 15:00. Equivalent unambiguous English date and time formats are allowed. Doors and performance require distinct labels. Missing assets or information, incorrect associations, unreadably brief sequences or a different duration fail.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation contains at least eight pages and recognisably reuses every listed earlier deliverable, including distinct examples for both stops. Still frames visibly representing the delivered announcement satisfy video coverage. Scaling and arranging work within presentation pages are allowed; merely naming an omitted deliverable or substituting unrelated artwork does not count.

The presentation explicitly identifies how title emphasis and practical-information ordering from the rules board appear in the posters, tickets and signs. Captions, annotations or explanatory prose may provide the evidence. The explanation must agree with the visible work; a gallery without this explanation or claims contradicted by the applications fail.

The presentation repeats the specification's complete-mark treatment, upright diamond and wave-band requirement, audience introduction and printed #8A2534. The complete company mark appears within the document, with page-level placement allowed to vary. Production and asset statements agree with the client facts. Wherever a stop is described, its venue, date, separately labelled doors time and performance time match the supplied Alder or Bracken record. Equivalent unambiguous English date and time formats are allowed; omissions of required repeated facts or contradictory records fail.

Where narrative imagery is used, it should present an original non-portrait interpretation of this production. Abstract, object-based or environmental storytelling is acceptable, and narrative illustration is not mandatory. Portrait-led story imagery fails; visual review alone does not establish authorship provenance.

Record all three supplied image-input roles: 03-riverthread-wordmark.png is the identity input; 04-costume-pattern.png is the constraint input; 05-backstage-materials.png is the reference input. The existing Inputs line already names the atmosphere reference. It informs tactile atmosphere without requiring literal reproduction of fabric, wood or lighting in every application; this diagnostic imposes no additional deliverable or failure condition.

The applications consistently implement the specification's complete-mark treatment and required upright diamond and pale wave-band motif while allowing application-specific composition and scale. Both stops' posters, tickets and entrance signs carry forward the rules board's production-title and practical-information hierarchy, including the distinction between doors and performance. The key visual and both posters repeat the audience introduction recorded in the specification.
